examples.ko: 그는 경찰의 출석 요구에 불응했어요.
examples.en: He did not comply with the police's request to appear.

examples.ko: 소환에 불응하면 강제로 조사받을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you refuse the summons, you may be questioned by force.

examples.ko: 회사의 부당한 지시에 불응한 직원이 있어요.
examples.en: There is an employee who refused the company's unfair order.

examples.ko: 몇 차례 요청에도 불응해서 결국 법원에 갔어요.
examples.en: They ignored several requests, so in the end we went to court.

examples.ko: 명령에 불응하는 사람은 규정에 따라 처리돼요.
examples.en: People who disobey the order are dealt with according to the rules.

examples.ko: 검사의 연락에 계속 불응하고 있어요.
examples.en: He keeps ignoring the prosecutor's contact.

explain: 요구, 명령, 소환, 요청처럼 따라야 하는 것에 따르지 않을 때 '~에 불응하다'로 써요. 반대말은 '응하다'예요. 뉴스나 공문에서 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '안 따르다', '거절하다'를 더 많이 써요.

phrases.en: He refused to obey the order to disperse.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명령'처럼 따라야 하는 것과 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs with things that must be obeyed, like orders.

phrases.en: If you don't comply, you must pay a fine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공문이나 안내문에서 자주 보이는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in official notices and documents.

phrases.en: The company did not comply with that demand.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불응하다'보다 부드럽고 일상에서도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softer than 불응하다 and usable in daily conversation too.

explain_en: It is used as '~에 불응하다' when someone does not follow something they are expected to follow, such as a demand, order, summons or request. The opposite is '응하다'. It appears often in the news and official documents, while everyday talk prefers '안 따르다' or '거절하다'.

t90.ax: He keeps ignoring the prosecutor's contact.

en: to be unreasonable; to be illogical

examples.ko: 이 규칙은 너무 불합리해서 따르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This rule is so unreasonable that it is hard to follow.

examples.ko: 불합리한 일을 보면 가만히 있기 어려워요.
examples.en: When I see something unreasonable, it is hard to stay silent.

examples.ko: 신입에게만 일이 몰리는 건 불합리하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't it unreasonable that all the work piles up on the newcomer?

examples.ko: 불합리하다고 느끼면 의견을 말해도 돼요.
examples.en: If you feel something is unreasonable, you can say what you think.

examples.ko: 결과가 같은데 보상이 다르다니 불합리해요.
examples.en: The result is the same but the reward is different, so it is unreasonable.

examples.ko: 불합리하게 오른 가격에 손님들이 항의했어요.
examples.en: Customers complained about the unreasonably raised price.

explain: '불공평'은 대우나 몫이 다를 때, '불합리하다'는 이유나 기준이 말이 안 될 때 어울려요. 반대는 '합리적이다'예요. 규칙, 제도, 가격, 대우를 비판할 때 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Unreasonable systems should be changed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 제도, 규칙, 대우를 비판할 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation when criticizing systems, rules, or treatment.

phrases.en: I think that rule is unreasonable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 의견을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form used to state your own opinion.

phrases.en: That decision is not reasonable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불합리하다'보다 부드럽게 말하는 반대 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer way to say it, using the opposite word.

explain_en: '불공평' fits when treatment or shares differ, while '불합리하다' fits when the reason or standard makes no sense. The opposite is '합리적이다'. It is often used when criticizing rules, systems, prices, or treatment.

t90.ax: This rule is so unreasonable that it is hard to follow.

examples.ko: 죄수가 감옥에서 가족에게 편지를 썼어요.
examples.en: The prisoner wrote a letter to his family from jail.

examples.ko: 영화 속 죄수는 결국 탈출에 성공했어요.
examples.en: The prisoner in the movie finally managed to escape.

examples.ko: 그 죄수를 다른 교도소로 옮긴대요.
examples.en: They say that prisoner is being moved to another prison.

examples.ko: 죄수 번호가 적힌 옷을 입고 있었어요.
examples.en: He was wearing clothes with a prisoner number on them.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 갇혀 있던 죄수들이 풀려났어요.
examples.en: The prisoners who had been locked up for a long time were released.

examples.ko: 그 소설의 주인공은 억울한 죄수였어요.
examples.en: The main character of that novel was a wrongly convicted prisoner.

explain: 뉴스나 공식적인 글에서는 '수감자', '재소자'를 더 많이 써요. '죄수'는 영화, 소설, 역사 이야기에 자주 나와요. 실제 사람을 가리킬 때는 조금 거칠게 들릴 수 있어요.

phrases.en: An actor in a prisoner's uniform appeared in the movie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 죄수가 입는 옷을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the clothes a prisoner wears.

phrases.en: The police are looking for the escaped prisoner.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감옥에서 도망친 사람을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for someone who escaped from prison.

phrases.en: The inmate met his family.
phrases.nuance_ko: '죄수'보다 덜 거칠어서 뉴스나 공식적인 글에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less harsh than '죄수'; more common in news and formal writing.

explain_en: In news and official writing, 수감자 and 재소자 are used more often. 죄수 shows up a lot in movies, novels and history stories. Used about a real person, it can sound a bit harsh.

t90.ax: The prisoner wrote a letter to his family from jail.

en: to solicit a favor (often improperly); to lobby

examples.ko: 회사 사람에게 승진을 청탁하다가 문제가 됐어요.
examples.en: It became a problem when someone asked a person at the company for an improper promotion favor.

examples.ko: 시험 문제를 알려 달라고 청탁하는 것은 불법이에요.
examples.en: Asking in secret for the exam questions is illegal.

examples.ko: 그 의원은 일을 청탁한 적이 없다고 말했어요.
examples.en: That lawmaker said they had never asked for any favor.

examples.ko: 돈을 주고 취직을 청탁하면 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pay money to arrange a job through a favor, you can be punished.

examples.ko: 잡지사가 작가에게 글을 청탁하고 있어요.
examples.en: The magazine company is commissioning a writer to write a piece.

examples.ko: 부정하게 청탁하지 않도록 규칙을 만들었어요.
examples.en: They made rules to prevent improper requests for favors.

explain: 청탁하다는 보통 법이나 규칙을 어기면서 부탁한다는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. '부탁하다'는 누구에게나 쓰지만 청탁은 뉴스에서 '부정 청탁', '인사 청탁'처럼 나와요. 잡지사가 작가에게 글을 부탁할 때는 나쁜 뜻 없이 '원고를 청탁하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 부정 청탁을 하면 처벌받을 수 있어요.
phrases.en: You can be punished for making an improper request.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청탁'을 명사로 쓴 대표적인 말로, 법이나 규칙을 어기는 부탁을 뜻해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical noun phrase with 청탁, meaning an improper favor that breaks rules or law; common in the news.

phrases.example: 그 공무원은 청탁을 받고 일을 처리해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The official handled the matter after receiving a request for a favor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청탁하다'의 반대쪽에서 부탁을 받는 사람의 입장으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the receiving side of a 청탁, from the viewpoint of the person who is asked.

phrases.en: He asked a friend for a job as a favor.
phrases.nuance_ko: '청탁하다'의 과거형 해요체예요. 평범한 부탁이 아니라 '뒤에서 부탁했다'는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past polite form of 청탁하다; it carries a sense of asking behind the scenes, not a normal request.

explain_en: 청탁하다 usually carries a bad feel of asking for a favor in a way that breaks laws or rules. 부탁하다 can be used with anyone, but 청탁 appears in news as 부정 청탁 (improper solicitation) or 인사 청탁 (personnel favor). When a magazine asks a writer for a piece, 원고를 청탁하다 has no negative meaning.

examples.ko: 경쟁 회사가 우리 팀 직원을 포섭하려고 했어요.
examples.en: A rival company tried to win over a member of our team.

examples.ko: 그가 돈으로 증인을 포섭했다는 의심을 받아요.
examples.en: He is suspected of winning over a witness with money.

examples.ko: 후보는 젊은 층을 포섭하기 위해 새 공약을 냈어요.
examples.en: The candidate put out a new pledge to win over young voters.

examples.ko: 아무리 저를 포섭하려 해도 소용없어요.
examples.en: No matter how hard you try to win me over, it's useless.

examples.ko: 영화 속 스파이는 친구를 포섭해서 정보를 얻어요.
examples.en: The spy in the movie recruits a friend to get information.

examples.ko: 상대 팀 선수를 포섭하는 건 규칙 위반이에요.
examples.en: Luring over a player from the other team breaks the rules.

explain: 일상에서는 '내 편으로 만들다', '끌어들이다'처럼 말하는 경우가 많아요. '누구를 포섭하다'처럼 대상에 '을/를'을 쓰고, 좋은 뜻보다는 몰래 내 편으로 만드는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: My friend was won over by the other team.
phrases.nuance_ko: '포섭하다'의 피동형으로, 남의 편으로 끌려갔다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form: someone was drawn to another side.

phrases.en: He was recruited by a bad group.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않았는데 끌려갔다는 피해의 느낌이 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a stronger sense of being a victim of the recruitment.
phrases.en_equiv: to be recruited against one's will

phrases.example: 그는 선물로 동료들을 자기 편으로 만들려고 했어요.
phrases.en: He tried to win his coworkers over to his side with gifts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 '포섭하다' 대신 쉽게 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday, easier way to say 'posubhada'.

explain_en: In daily speech people often say '내 편으로 만들다' or '끌어들이다' instead. The target takes '을/를', as in '누구를 포섭하다', and it often has a feel of quietly bringing someone to your side rather than a purely positive tone.

en: to resist; to defy; to disobey

examples.ko: 시민들은 부당한 명령에 항거했어요.
examples.en: The citizens stood up against the unjust order.

examples.ko: 그는 불의에 항거하다가 감옥에 갔어요.
examples.en: He went to prison for resisting injustice.

examples.ko: 학생들이 독재에 항거하며 거리로 나왔어요.
examples.en: Students came out into the streets to protest against the dictatorship.

examples.ko: 일제에 항거한 독립운동가들을 기억해야 해요.
examples.en: We must remember the independence activists who resisted Japanese rule.

examples.ko: 사람들은 권력에 항거할 용기를 냈어요.
examples.en: People found the courage to defy those in power.

examples.ko: 부당한 대우에 항거하는 파업이 이어졌어요.
examples.en: Strikes protesting the unfair treatment continued.

explain: '~에 항거하다'처럼 권력이나 불의 같은 큰 힘에 맞서 저항한다는 뜻이라 역사나 뉴스에서 주로 써요. '저항하다'와 비슷하지만 더 무겁고 글에 어울리는 말이에요. 일상에서는 '맞서다', '반발하다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Citizens took to the streets to resist the dictatorship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 권력에 맞서는 상황에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing in situations of standing against power.

phrases.en: He went on a hunger strike as a sign of protest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대하는 마음을 행동으로 보여 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when showing opposition through an action.

phrases.en: The residents resisted the development plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항거하다보다 덜 무겁고 쓰임이 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Less heavy than 항거하다 and used more widely.

explain_en: Used as '~에 항거하다', it means standing against a big force such as power or injustice, so it mostly appears in history and news. It is similar to '저항하다' but heavier and more suited to writing. In daily talk, '맞서다' or '반발하다' sounds more natural.

t90.ax: He went to prison for resisting injustice.

examples.ko: 면접관이 제 긴장한 마음을 간파했어요.
examples.en: The interviewer saw through my nervousness.

examples.ko: 감독은 상대 팀의 작전을 간파하고 선수를 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The coach saw through the other team's tactics and swapped a player.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 거짓말을 금방 간파해요.
examples.en: That friend can see through a lie right away.

examples.ko: 엄마는 제 속마음을 단번에 간파하셨어요.
examples.en: My mom saw through my true feelings at once.

examples.ko: 상황을 빨리 간파하는 사람이 일도 잘해요.
examples.en: People who read a situation quickly also do their work well.

examples.ko: 문제의 핵심을 간파하지 못해서 시간이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: I couldn't grasp the core of the problem, so it took time.

explain: '알아채다'가 일상 대화의 말이라면 '간파하다'는 숨은 의도, 속임수, 약점을 꿰뚫어 볼 때 써요. 글이나 뉴스, 스포츠 해설에서 자주 나와요. 윗사람이 하면 '간파하시다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: My friend saw through my true feelings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨기고 있던 마음을 알아챌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone notices feelings you were hiding.
phrases.en_equiv: to see through someone's true feelings

phrases.en: He immediately saw through the other side's intention.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대가 숨긴 목적을 꿰뚫어 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when seeing through someone's hidden purpose.

phrases.en: I was embarrassed because my lie was seen through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내 속임수나 약점을 남에게 들켰다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means your trick or weakness was caught by someone else.

explain_en: '알아채다' is the everyday word, while '간파하다' is for seeing through a hidden intention, trick or weakness. You often meet it in writing, news and sports commentary. For a respected person, say '간파하시다'.

en: to be gullible; to take someone's words at face value

examples.ko: 그냥 한 농담인데 곧이듣지 마세요.
examples.en: It was just a joke, so don't take it seriously.

examples.ko: 동생은 제 말을 다 곧이들어요.
examples.en: My younger brother believes everything I say.

examples.ko: 친구가 장난으로 한 말을 곧이듣고 울었어요.
examples.en: She took her friend's joking words at face value and cried.

examples.ko: 광고에 나오는 말을 다 곧이들으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't believe everything that ads say.

examples.ko: 그 사람 말은 곧이듣기 어려워요.
examples.en: That person's words are hard to believe.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 어른들 말을 무엇이든 곧이들었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I believed whatever adults told me.

explain: '곧이듣지 마세요'처럼 부정형으로 가장 많이 써요. 거짓말이나 농담을 의심 없이 그대로 믿는 느낌이 있어서 '믿다'와는 달리 속을 수 있다는 뉘앙스가 있어요. 'ㄷ' 불규칙이라 '곧이들어요', '곧이들으면'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 그 사람 말은 곧이들으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't take what that person says at face value.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조건 '-(으)면'과 같이 써서 믿지 말라고 조언할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)면' to advise someone not to believe something.
phrases.en_equiv: you shouldn't take it at face value

phrases.en: I believed that lie completely.
phrases.nuance_ko: 속아서 그대로 믿었다는 과거 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A past form meaning one was fooled and believed it as it was.

phrases.en: There are people who take jokes seriously.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 활용형이고 쉽게 믿는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before nouns, describing someone who believes easily.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, like '곧이듣지 마세요'. Unlike plain '믿다', it carries a feel of believing something without doubt, so you might be fooled. It is a 'ㄷ' irregular verb: '곧이들어요', '곧이들으면'.

examples.ko: 담력이 큰 아이라서 밤길도 무서워하지 않아요.
examples.en: He is a gutsy kid, so he isn't afraid of night roads.

examples.ko: 놀이공원에서 무서운 놀이기구로 담력을 시험했어요.
examples.en: I tested my nerve on the scary rides at the amusement park.

examples.ko: 담력을 키우려고 일부러 사람들 앞에서 노래했어요.
examples.en: To build up my nerve, I sang in front of people on purpose.

examples.ko: 그는 담력 하나는 누구에게도 안 져요.
examples.en: When it comes to guts, he loses to no one.

examples.ko: 캠프에서 담력 훈련으로 밤길을 혼자 걸었어요.
examples.en: At camp, we walked a night path alone as a nerve-training activity.

examples.ko: 담력 없는 사람은 공포 영화를 못 봐요.
examples.en: People without nerve can't watch horror movies.

explain: 겁내지 않고 버티는 마음의 힘이에요. '용기'보다 무서운 상황에서 겁먹지 않는 느낌이 강하고, 비슷한 말로 '배짱'이 있어요. '담력이 세다/크다', '담력 훈련'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: That child is fearless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겁이 없는 사람을 말할 때 가장 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to describe a fearless person.

phrases.en: We did a courage-building activity at summer camp.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무서운 상황을 견디는 연습이나 놀이를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to practice or games for enduring scary situations.

phrases.en: That person has plenty of guts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 겁 없이 밀고 나가는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word, with a sense of boldly pushing ahead.

explain_en: It is the inner strength to hold steady without fear. Compared with '용기', it leans toward not getting scared in frightening situations, and '배짱' is a similar word. It is used as '담력이 세다/크다' or '담력 훈련'.

t90.ax: When it comes to guts, he loses to no one.

en: to be satisfactory; to be acceptable

examples.ko: 새로 정한 규칙이 영 마뜩하지 않아요.
examples.en: I'm not at all happy with the newly set rule.

examples.ko: 그 제안이 그리 마뜩해 보이지는 않았어요.
examples.en: That proposal didn't seem all that satisfying.

examples.ko: 사장님은 내 계획이 마뜩지 않으신 눈치예요.
examples.en: The boss seems not to like my plan.

examples.ko: 마뜩한 집을 찾을 때까지 계속 보러 다녔어요.
examples.en: I kept going to see places until I found a house I liked.

examples.ko: 월급은 괜찮은데 일하는 분위기가 마뜩하지 않아요.
examples.en: The pay is fine, but I'm not happy with the work atmosphere.

examples.ko: 마뜩한 선물이 없어서 고르기 힘들어요.
examples.en: There's no gift that suits me, so it's hard to choose.

explain: 대부분 '마뜩하지 않다', '마뜩잖다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 '마음에 차지 않는다'는 느낌을 줘요. '마음에 들다'보다 조금 점잖고 글에서 더 잘 보이는 말이에요. 긍정으로 '마뜩한 집'처럼 쓸 수는 있지만 흔하지는 않아요.

phrases.en: I'm not at all happy with that plan.
phrases.nuance_ko: '마뜩하지 않다'의 줄임말로 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The contracted form of '마뜩하지 않다,' and the more common one.

phrases.en: He shook his head with a dissatisfied look.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음에 차지 않는 얼굴을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a face that shows dissatisfaction.

phrases.en: My parents don't think much of my choice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 생각이나 행동을 못마땅해할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when disapproving of someone's idea or action.

explain_en: It is mostly used with a negative, as in '마뜩하지 않다' or '마뜩잖다', giving the feeling that something doesn't satisfy you. It sounds a bit more formal than '마음에 들다' and shows up more in writing. A positive use like '마뜩한 집' is possible but not common.

t90.ax: The boss seems not to like my plan.

examples.ko: 설마하니 그 사람이 거짓말을 했을까요?
examples.en: Surely that person wouldn't have lied, would they?

examples.ko: 설마하니 벌써 밥을 다 먹었어요?
examples.en: You can't possibly have finished eating already, can you?

examples.ko: 설마하니 이렇게 비가 오는데 나오겠어요?
examples.en: Surely they won't come out when it's raining this hard, right?

examples.ko: 설마하니 이렇게 일찍 올 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I never thought you would come this early.

examples.ko: 설마하니 그 친구가 그런 일까지 하겠어요?
examples.en: Surely that friend wouldn't go so far as to do that, would he?

examples.ko: 설마하니 내 생일을 잊은 건 아니겠죠?
examples.en: You didn't forget my birthday, did you?

explain: '설마'를 조금 더 강조한 말이에요. 뒤에 '~겠어요?', '~ㄹ까요?'처럼 그럴 리 없다는 추측이나 의문이 와요. 말할 때는 보통 짧게 '설마'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Surely you didn't skip your homework?
phrases.nuance_ko: '설마하니'보다 짧고 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is shorter than 설마하니 and used more often in daily conversation.

phrases.en: Surely he didn't walk all that long way, did he?
phrases.nuance_ko: '~겠어요?'와 함께 써서 그럴 리 없다는 마음을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with ~겠어요? to show you think it's unlikely.

phrases.en: I thought surely not, but he really came.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그럴 리 없다고 생각했는데 사실이 된 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when something you doubted turns out to be true.

explain_en: It is a slightly stronger form of '설마'. It is followed by a doubtful guess or question, such as '~겠어요?' or '~ㄹ까요?', meaning it surely can't be so. In speech people usually just say '설마'.

t90.ax: You didn't forget my birthday, did you?

examples.ko: 아이들은 장난감에 대한 소유욕이 강해요.
examples.en: Children have a strong desire to own their toys.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 소유욕이 너무 커서 친구를 잃었어요.
examples.en: He was so possessive that he lost his friends.

examples.ko: 물건에 대한 소유욕 없이 가볍게 살아요.
examples.en: I live lightly, without a desire to own things.

examples.ko: 소유욕도 지나치면 관계가 불편해져요.
examples.en: Possessiveness makes a relationship uncomfortable when it goes too far.

examples.ko: 강아지도 소유욕을 보일 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Even puppies show possessiveness sometimes.

examples.ko: 소유욕과 사랑을 헷갈리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't confuse possessiveness with love.

explain: 물건을 갖고 싶은 마음뿐 아니라 사람을 자기 곁에 두고 싶어 하는 마음에도 써요. '소유욕이 강하다', '소유욕이 없다'처럼 말하고, 사람에게 쓸 때는 부정적인 느낌이 있어요. 비슷한 '독점욕'은 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음에 더 초점이 있어요.

phrases.en: Seeing the pretty bowl made me want to own it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갖고 싶은 마음이 새로 들었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a desire to own something newly arises.
phrases.en_equiv: to feel a desire to own

phrases.example: 독점욕이 강해서 친구가 다른 사람과 놀면 싫어해요.
phrases.en: He is so possessive that he dislikes it when his friend plays with others.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소유욕' 중에서도 혼자만 차지하고 싶은 마음을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A type of possessiveness: wanting to keep something all to oneself.

phrases.en: If you let go of possessiveness, your mind feels easier.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갖고 싶은 마음을 내려놓는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means letting go of the urge to own.

explain_en: It covers not only wanting to own things but also wanting to keep a person close to you. People say '소유욕이 강하다' or '소유욕이 없다', and when used about people it sounds negative. The similar '독점욕' focuses more on wanting to have something all to yourself.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 낮의 더위가 조금 수그러들었어요.
examples.en: When the rain came, the daytime heat eased a little.

examples.ko: 시간이 지나자 화가 조금 수그러들었어요.
examples.en: As time passed, my anger died down a bit.

examples.ko: 그 논란은 쉽게 수그러들지 않아요.
examples.en: That controversy isn't dying down easily.

examples.ko: 바람이 수그러들면 배가 출발할 거예요.
examples.en: Once the wind dies down, the boat will leave.

examples.ko: 유행이 수그러들 때까지 기다려 봐요.
examples.en: Let's wait until the trend dies down.

examples.ko: 열이 수그러들어서 이제 좀 괜찮아요.
examples.en: My fever has gone down, so I'm okay now.

explain: 기세, 열, 화, 논란, 더위처럼 강하던 것이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '가라앉다'보다 '세던 것이 꺾인다'는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: The heat just won't die down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 약해지지 않고 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something keeps going without weakening.

phrases.en: When the rain came, the fire's force died down.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 번지던 것의 힘이 줄어들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the force of something strong weakens.

phrases.en: The controversy will die down in time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 이야기에서 시끄럽던 일이 조용해질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a noisy issue quiets down.

explain_en: Use it when something strong, such as momentum, fever, anger, controversy or heat, gradually weakens. Compared with '가라앉다', it feels more like something forceful losing its edge.

t90.ax: Let's wait until the trend dies down.

examples.ko: 이번 경기는 우리 팀에게 승산이 충분히 있어요.
examples.en: We have plenty of chance of winning this game.

examples.ko: 솔직히 말하면 이번 대결의 승산은 반반이에요.
examples.en: Honestly, the chance of winning this match is fifty-fifty.

examples.ko: 승산 없는 싸움은 처음부터 하지 않는 게 나아요.
examples.en: It's better not to start a fight you can't win from the beginning.

examples.ko: 승산을 높이려면 연습을 더 해야 해요.
examples.en: To raise your chances of winning, you have to practice more.

examples.ko: 승산도 없는데 왜 도전하느냐고 물었어요.
examples.en: I asked why he was taking the challenge when he had no chance of winning.

examples.ko: 승산이 보이자 선수들의 표정이 밝아졌어요.
examples.en: When a chance of winning appeared, the players' faces brightened.

explain: '승산이 있다/없다', '승산이 높다/낮다'처럼 말해요. 이길 가능성을 따져 볼 때 쓰고, 경기뿐 아니라 협상이나 도전에도 써요. '승률'은 지금까지 이긴 비율이라서 앞으로의 가능성을 말하는 '승산'과 달라요.

phrases.en: This fight has no chance of winning from the start.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이기기 어렵다고 판단할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for judging that winning is unlikely.
phrases.en_equiv: to have no chance of winning

phrases.example: 준비를 많이 해서 이번에는 승산이 높아요.
phrases.en: I prepared a lot, so my chances of winning are high this time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이길 가능성이 크다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the chance of winning is good.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a high chance of winning

phrases.example: 일을 시작하기 전에 승산을 따져 봤어요.
phrases.en: Before starting, I weighed my chances of success.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이길 가능성이 있는지 계산해 볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when calculating whether there's a chance to win.

explain_en: You say '승산이 있다/없다' or '승산이 높다/낮다'. It is used when judging the chance of winning, not only in games but also in negotiations and challenges. '승률' is the ratio of wins so far, which differs from '승산', which is about future chances.
